program: Community-led environmental health, leadership and policy advocacy
priceScope: Conditional full annual recipient cost against partial environmental-policy benefits; unmeasured direct and other program effects remain unknown, not whole-portfolio or next-gift expected value.

what: Cultivando supports Latino community leadership, emotional wellness and environmental-health advocacy in North Denver and Commerce City.
Its 2025 report describes coalition participation in air-toxics rulemaking, not measured emissions or clinical health improvements.
The conditional initial reference tests a finite local policy channel with health and signed household, participant and payer effects.
strengths: Current native activities and legal recipient are verified from original reporting.
Coalition participation has a concrete rulemaking mechanism beyond monitoring alone.
Separate participant and downstream-beneficiary cohorts avoid charging every hypothetical resident advocacy costs.
reservations: Monitoring and adopted standards do not establish implemented abatement or recipient causal share.
The 10,000 potential residents and utility/resource coefficients are explicit hypotheses.
Whole annual cost includes direct programs and fiscal sponsorship whose benefits are unpriced here.

sections.what: Cultivando, EIN 84-1499624, combines promotoras, community education, family/emotional wellness and environmental advocacy. Current 2025 reporting includes formal COCA coalition participation in Regulation 30, community testimony and tours near Suncor. National training in San Antonio is outside the Denver reference. Donation page links an owned Pay Pal hosted button, with no transaction performed.
sections.monitoring: The 2025 PDF reports 20+coalition leaders and 30+testimonies, five priority air-toxics standards and Hydrogen Sulfide inclusion. These are participation and rulemaking claims, not reduced exposure, completed abatement, cancer prevention or sole-recipient impact. Planned 2026 health survey is not an existing controlled outcome. Other 50 women,313 workshop participants,14 FFNgraduates and 20 homevisits are not added as unique clinical beneficiaries. The official AQCC 2024–2025 report independently confirms priority-air-toxic benchmarks adopted in September 2025 under the legislative mandate; it does not establish Cultivando's causal contribution or implemented exposure reduction.
sections.qualitative: The policy reference hypothesizes 10,000 local residents, .3 implementation and .15 incremental recipient attribution, .003 healthyyear/resident/year over 3 years after 2 years delay. All are unmeasured judgments, not conversions from cancer-risk thresholds. Existing regulation, public enforcement and other coalition members are alternatives. .5 household resource proxy is judged;30 engaged household-equivalent advocates are distinct from the hypothetical downstream population.
sections.cost: Full FY 2025 cost is $1,508,452. Center yields 3.704403 health QALYs and .486624 signed income-equivalent years, about $3.60 M per better life. $100 net household resources after tax/benefits/compliance effects are halved only if positive. All 30 engaged participants retain $10 current effort cost and health stress even if policy fails; implemented-policy payer compliance $20,000 and 20 worker households losing $1,000 are distinct judged incidence, gated by incremental implementation. Current-year effort and delayed gain are not capitalized together; same-year participant gains/costs are joint logs. These are hypotheses, not measured pollution-driven work returns.
sections.funding: Original full costs: FY 2023$1,603,171, FY 2024$1,653,391, FY 2025$1,508,452. FY 2025$333,654 Fortaleza Familiar fiscal sponsorship ended after its independent charity recognition. Full numerator includes that program, whose benefits are unknown here; excluding this transfer is a boundary sensitivity, not an adjusted whole-portfolio evaluation. Environmental-program recognized cost $432,384 is another partial-scope sensitivity excluding overhead, direct programs and unpaid resources. Annual report revenue $1,132,325 is not an expense estimate; actual next-dollar capacity requires confirmation.

sources.title: 2025 primary annual report and rulemaking participation

model.costScope: Whole FY 2025 recognized recipient cost including sponsorship, against one policy benefit channel. Environmental cost 432384 and excluding 333654 sponsorship are scope diagnostics, not complete marginal cost.
model.geographicAttribution: Potential residents are explicitly local North Denver/Commerce City CBSA 19740 hypothesis; g 1 represents that chosen local channel, not all organizational work. Texas and other nonlocal program benefits excluded as unknown.
model.formula: Policy b=implementation×recipient incremental attribution. Health=(N×b×q×finite delayed duration−engaged×current harm)×Denver share. Delayed household resources and current participant costs are separate actual-year logs; same-year overlapping participants use joint gain minus cost. Distinct compliance/worker losses are implementation-gated and localized once. Price=10 C/(health+signed income).
model.counterfactual: Existing regulatory enforcement, baseline industry obligations, other COCA coalition members and public services absent added recipient advocacy.
model.attribution: Separate .3 implementation probability and .15 incremental recipient share, both judgment; benchmark adoption is not proof of implemented emission reduction.
model.uncertainty: No measured emissions attributable to recipient, local population/dose, clinical utility, work/resource or compliance incidence; finite delayed and failed-policy regimes tested.
model.nativeOutcomes: 2025 coalition participation 20+leaders/30+testimonies, standards/rulemaking claims and community programs. No delivered causal emission-health cohort.
